season.evidence: Web: July through early October most reliable; June has snow on the trail above Slate Pass and slushy snow at Freds Pass; a late Sep/early Oct party met two feet of snow at Slate Pass. Ascent histogram peaks Jul-Sep.

track.why: Only stored route; logged route S face to SW ridge from Slate Pass via Freds/Doris Lake on 29 Aug 2024; report describes rising traverse from Doris Lake, south-side talus, SW ridge class 2 and descent by that ridge, matching ours. Start 23 m from the Slate Pass pin, reaches summit 15 m. NOTE: the recorded line keeps going after the summit toward Eureka Creek (ends 13 km away), so use only trailhead-to-summit.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Complete loop but a four-day six-peak slam; would draw far more than this route.
Late June, 486 m start, in the snow shoulder season.

facts.text: In late June the trail north of Slate Pass can be snow-covered down to about 6,400 ft and the pass above Freds Lake held slushy snow.
In mid-July the trail to Lake Doris is in good shape, with a ford of the Middle Fork Pasayten and some blowdowns on the Eureka Creek trail.
Stash overnight packs near 7,300 ft; the direct south slope is heavy loose talus, the southwest ridge crest gives class 2 footing.
Descend the southwest ridge to the saddle, then drop scree back to your packs; this is easier than reversing the boulder field.
Gaiters (loose scree on the upper slopes in July)

notes: Track 2630332 oneway: truncate at the summit. 2970242 is a big multi-peak loop and should not be used.
